name: slack_channel
title: Slack
description: Your Slack: a Slack sign-in (acts as you), or your own Slack app's user token, or a bot token.
needed_for: Reads your Slack — everything you are in, or one channel — into conversations and replies there.
justification: A Slack source reads conversations and posts replies. A sign-in or your own app's user token acts as you across everything you are in; a bot token acts as that bot only where it was invited.

SLACK_SIGNIN.label: Sign in with Slack
SLACK_SIGNIN.hint: Acts as you: replies are posted under your name.

SLACK_USER_TOKEN.label: User OAuth Token
SLACK_USER_TOKEN.hint: Your own Slack app's User OAuth Token (OAuth & Permissions). Acts as you.

SLACK_BOT_TOKEN.label: Bot token
SLACK_BOT_TOKEN.hint: Your Slack app's Bot User OAuth Token (OAuth & Permissions). Replies come from the bot.

SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL.label: Request URL
SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL.hint: Your own app's Request URL, held by Flowpad cloud (flow source step public-webhook). Not a secret.

signin.label: Sign in with Slack (acts as you)
signin.hint: One click: everything you are in — DMs, group DMs, channels — read and answered as you.

app.label: Your own app (acts as you, live)
app.hint: An app you create in your workspace; its User OAuth Token acts as you, and its Request URL delivers live.

bot.label: Your own bot
bot.hint: Paste the bot token of a Slack app you created.
